content.user_title: Delegate Tasks and Verify Team Deliverables
content.value_statement: Unclear assignments and scattered feedback make team delivery difficult to verify. This skill creates task briefs, coordinates authorized follow-up, and checks deliverables against agreed criteria.
actual_capabilities: Compare task requirements with authorized local personnel evidence, while identifying unknown availability and capability gaps.
Create forwardable task briefs with deliverables, scope, acceptance criteria, timing, dependencies, and feedback instructions.
Use verified Feishu CLI capabilities for authorized task creation, document reading, replies, and notifications.
Persist task records and evidence-backed state transitions in a project-specific local SQLite database.
Deduplicate and merge registered document edit events, then invoke an explicitly enabled synchronous worker through JSON stdin.
Review available deliverables against original criteria and report verified results, missing evidence, blockers, and owner decisions.
limitations: Automatic follow-up requires configured Feishu permissions, document subscriptions, a persistent listener, a dispatcher, a trusted worker, and a verified notification route.
The bundled runtime manages records and queues; it does not implement an Agent worker or built-in Codex desktop or Grok notification interfaces.
Real-account subscriptions and complete business workflows still require local integration testing; offline tests do not establish production readiness.
The workflow excludes recruitment, employee ranking, punishment, and unauthorized payment, publication, or business commitments.

use_cases.title: Prepare a manual delegation
use_cases.description: Turn a task and existing personnel notes into a forwardable brief with clear outcomes, evidence requirements, and negotiable timing.

use_cases.title: Review a submitted deliverable
use_cases.description: Compare accessible work with the original acceptance criteria, identify missing evidence, and prepare a concise owner report.

use_cases.title: Connect an authorized follow-up queue
use_cases.description: Configure registered document events and a trusted synchronous worker, with explicit execution approval and manual reconciliation after uncertain results.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a task brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs-human-dispatch to delegate [task] to [person]. Include deliverables, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a deadline marked pending negotiation when unknown. Return forwardable text only; do not send messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a delegation without external tools.

prompt_templates.title: Assess potential assignees
prompt_templates.prompt: Review only the authorized personnel files in [directory] for [task]. Compare capability evidence, unknown workload, and dependencies. Recommend a candidate and draft the brief without sending it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choose an assignee using existing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a submission
prompt_templates.prompt: For task [task ID], compare [submission] with [original acceptance criteria]. State the evidence and conclusion for each criterion. Draft feedback and an owner report; do not change scope, publish, or send notifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: distinguish submission from verified acceptance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare automatic follow-up
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare automatic follow-up for [registered task] using [absolute state directory] and [trusted worker command]. Check identity, permissions, document subscription, self identities, dispatch scheduling, and notification routing. Keep subscription in dry-run and do not start listeners or workers until I approve the full action scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: stage an event-driven workflow before enabling execution.

output_examples.input: Draft a text-only assignment for Maya to write a product overview. Require audience, features, and limitations sections; timing is not yet agreed.
output: Task ID: product-overview-01. Assignee: Maya. Mode: text. State: draft; nothing has been sent.
Deliverable: a product overview covering audience, features, and limitations.
Acceptance: each required section is present; product claims match the supplied materials.
Timing: pending negotiation. Maya should confirm availability, dependencies, and a proposed deadline.
Feedback: include the task ID and identify each update as acceptance, question, progress, blocker, or submission for review.

output_examples.input: Review task overview-02. All three required sections are present, but a mandatory source link is inaccessible. Do not send notifications.
output: Task overview-02: the required sections are present.
Source verification: incomplete because the mandatory link is inaccessible.
Conclusion: needs_revision. Provide an accessible source before acceptance.
Owner report: the draft meets the structural requirement; evidence verification remains blocked. No notification was sent.

best_practices: Agree on scope, observable acceptance criteria, timing, and feedback channels before assigning work.
Verify recipients, CLI permissions, and the full external action scope before enabling writes or automatic workers.
Use a protected absolute state directory for services, and reconcile actual external actions before retrying uncertain jobs.
anti_patterns: Treating document edits, queue insertion, process startup, or a submission claim as proof of completion or notification delivery.
Allowing employee text or event contents to change authorization, select executable commands, or expose unrelated personnel files.
Expanding acceptance criteria after submission, assuming overtime, or using task records to rank or punish employees.

faq.question: Can I use this without Feishu?
faq.answer: Yes. Text mode creates forwardable briefs and reviews feedback or deliverables supplied by the user.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Automatic follow-up requires a real synchronous worker configured for the chosen host.

faq.question: Where are task records stored?
faq.answer: The Python runtime stores records under ~/.dbs/human-dispatch/ in a project-specific directory. Use --state-dir to select another protected location.

faq.question: Does installation enable automatic monitoring?
faq.answer: No. Automatic follow-up requires verified permissions, subscriptions, persistent processes, a configured worker, and an authorized notification route.

faq.question: What happens when a worker result is uncertain?
faq.answer: The queue blocks further work for that task. Check actual external actions before resolving the job as processed or explicitly retrying.

faq.question: Does a submitted task automatically pass acceptance?
faq.answer: No. Deliverables must be checked against the original criteria. Missing access or evidence prevents a verified acceptance conclusion.
